name: Barakel
title: Elihu's father
summary: Barakel is known from the book of Job as the father of Elihu, the young man who spoke to Job and his three friends. He was of the line of Buz, which connects him to Abraham's lineage through Nahor. Barakel is mentioned only as the father of Elihu and has no independent role in the story.

keyEvents.title: Elihu, son of Barakel, is introduced
keyEvents.description: Elihu, son of Barakel from Buz, is introduced as the fourth and youngest speaker in the book of Job after Job's three friends failed to answer him.

keyEvents.title: Elihu's lineage is mentioned
keyEvents.description: Barakel is identified as a Buzite, which connects him to Buz, son of Abraham's brother Nahor, placing him in an acknowledged family line.

keyEvents.title: Elihu speaks on behalf of his father's lineage
keyEvents.description: Elihu, son of Barakel, begins his speech and defends God's justice toward Job, thus representing his father's lineage in this important theological discussion.

keyEvents.title: Elihu's Speech About God's Greatness
keyEvents.description: As the son of Barachel, Elihu conveys profound wisdom about God's justice and sovereignty, preparing the way for God's own answer to Job.

keyEvents.title: The Buzites' Connection to Abraham
keyEvents.description: Barachel's lineage from the family of Buz links him to Abraham's genealogical line through Nahor, Abraham's brother, who had a son named Buz.
